options.name: Extract-transform-load pipeline
options.description: Extract data, stage it, transform it, then load it into final storage.

options.name: Extract-load-transform pipeline
options.description: Extract data, load it before transformation, then transform it in the destination environment.

options.name: Data acquisition and ingestion mechanism
options.description: Acquire ML data from operational sources and move it through push-based, pull-based, or event-driven ingestion into preparation pipelines.

options.name: Composable transformation pipeline
options.description: Preparation is organized as immutable, reusable transformation stages that can be tested and recombined across data sources and processing steps.

options.name: Partitioned parallel pipeline
options.description: Preparation is organized into partitioned processing stages executed in parallel to scale feature and dataset processing.

options.name: Integrated adaptive preparation pipeline
options.description: Preparation combines composable transformations and scalable parallel execution with feedback from exploration and validation to refine data acquisition or ingestion.

options.name: Automated preprocessing and model training
options.description: Automates data preprocessing and recurring model training while leaving feature engineering outside the automated scope.

options.name: Automated feature engineering
options.description: Automates the generation of features during pipeline construction without also automating preprocessing, feature selection, or model training.

options.name: Automated feature engineering and selection
options.description: Automates both feature generation and the selection of useful features within the modeling workflow.

options.name: Automated preprocessing, feature engineering, and model training
options.description: Automates preprocessing, feature generation, and recurring model training as a coordinated ML pipeline.

options.name: AutoML-assisted preparation pipeline
options.description: Uses generalized AutoML pipeline automation together with automated preprocessing and feature engineering, while not necessarily automating feature selection or training as separate activities.

options.name: End-to-end automated ML pipeline
options.description: Automates the full preparation and modeling workflow, including preprocessing, feature engineering and selection, pipeline automation, internally scripted activities, and model training.

options.name: Centralized feature repository
options.description: Prepared features are maintained in one shared, consistently structured location for training, testing, production, and downstream use.

options.name: Online feature-serving store
options.description: Features are maintained in an online store optimized for low-latency access by real-time prediction workloads.

options.name: Synchronized multi-source feature preparation
options.description: Features are created by synchronizing or joining multiple upstream data sources, without prescribing a particular offline-to-online serving arrangement.

options.name: Offline-to-online feature-store pipeline
options.description: Features are retained offline and, where required, replicated into an online store for serving. This profile covers basic offline storage as well as explicit offline-to-online replication.

options.name: Synchronized offline-to-online feature pipeline
options.description: Multiple sources are synchronized to produce features that are retained offline and replicated or published to an online feature store for low-latency serving.

options.name: Integrated multi-repository feature topology
options.description: Feature ownership, storage, replication, synchronization, and result publication are integrated across microservice-owned sources, offline and online stores, and multiple repositories.

options.name: Shared feature-store abstraction
options.description: A centralized feature-store interface defines features and generates training data, without an explicitly combined multi-technology storage layer.

options.name: Polyglot feature-store storage architecture
options.description: A shared feature-store abstraction is implemented with complementary storage technologies, such as object, file, database, or key-value stores, for different feature and data-engineering needs.

options.name: Dependency-orchestrated workflow
options.description: An orchestration mechanism coordinates dependent ML tasks through explicit workflow dependencies and schedules them on compute infrastructure.

options.name: Script-led workflow with orchestration support
options.description: Practitioners coordinate ML steps primarily through manually executed scripts, optionally combining them with explicit task dependencies or infrastructure orchestration.

options.name: Continuous training with infrequent production release
options.description: Models are updated through a continuous or recurring training pipeline, but production releases occur only occasionally and may follow a manually coordinated lifecycle.

options.name: Continuous training cadence
options.description: Models are updated repeatedly as new examples or fresh data arrive, without specifying an infrequent production-release schedule as a separate facet.

options.name: Ingestion-completion triggering
options.description: Preparation starts when the ingestion service signals completion.

options.name: Batch-triggered execution
options.description: Processing functions are initiated as scheduled or dataset-oriented batch jobs.

options.name: Kafka-stream triggering
options.description: Processing functions are initiated by events arriving on Kafka or comparable streams.

options.name: Schedule-or-trigger production execution
options.description: Production training or execution starts on a schedule or in response to a trigger.

options.name: Model-decay retraining triggering
options.description: Initiate retraining when a model-decay measure indicates degraded performance.

options.name: New-data retraining triggering
options.description: Initiate retraining when newly available data satisfies the retraining condition.

options.name: Local notebook runtime
options.description: Processing is initially validated in a local notebook environment.

options.name: Fog-computing deployment architecture
options.description: Place machine-learning processing across distributed edge-oriented fog endpoints and cloud resources.

options.name: Network-endpoint execution
options.description: Execute machine-learning microservices close to distributed IoT data sources at network endpoints.

options.name: Nearline runtime location
options.description: Execution in an intermediate nearline regime between offline batch and real-time online serving.

options.name: External-cluster execution
options.description: Offload heavy ML calculations from local machines to externally connected clusters.

options.name: Cloud-hosted serving placement
options.description: Place model serving in a cloud-hosted web-service environment.

options.name: Local serving placement
options.description: Place model serving in a local deployment environment.

options.name: Edge-device serving placement
options.description: Place model serving on an edge device such as Azure IoT Edge.

options.name: Multi-mode Spark and engine runtime
options.description: Distributed computation is provisioned and operated through a combination of serverless Spark execution, operator-managed Spark clusters, and interchangeable computation engines.

options.name: Managed Spark runtime
options.description: Distributed Spark computation is operated through managed or orchestrated Spark execution, covering both serverless access and explicitly managed Spark clusters.

options.name: Self-healing multi-engine runtime
options.description: Distributed computation is operated across heterogeneous engines with fault-tolerant, self-healing execution and support for distributed Spark workloads.

options.name: Cluster-level elastic workload provisioning
options.description: Compute environments are explicitly configurable, sized for the workload, and able to scale as demand changes. This provides an integrated approach to provisioning cluster resources for ML processing and serving.

options.name: Elastic workload-specific resource sizing
options.description: Compute capacity is tailored to workload requirements and adjusted dynamically as demand changes, without necessarily prescribing a particular cluster configuration.

options.name: Workload-specific resource sizing
options.description: CPU, memory, or other compute allocations are selected according to the requirements of the workload or service, with sizing based on expected performance and load.

options.name: Profiled hardware-targeted resource provisioning
options.description: Deployment resources are configured and profiled for the service, including selection among CPU, GPU, or FPGA inference hardware according to model and performance requirements.

options.name: Serverless inference execution
options.description: Inference stages execute in a serverless function environment, without specifying a dedicated container or Kubernetes deployment target.

options.name: Container-trained, serverless-served execution
options.description: Training executes in a container-based environment and inference is served through a serverless function environment.

options.name: Container-orchestrated inference execution
options.description: Inference is deployed to a managed container or Kubernetes-based service, with training potentially executed in a container-based environment.

options.name: Function-oriented serverless workload automation
options.description: Package ML stages as executable functions and automate their serverless execution, including orchestration and operational handling. This option does not require explicit runtime dependency injection.

options.name: Dependency-injected ML runtime platform
options.description: Use a serverless, function-oriented runtime that also supplies parameters, secrets, credentials, connections, and datasets to workloads at execution time.

options.name: Python implementation-language profile
options.description: Python is used as the primary implementation language for machine-learning and data-science software, without a specified notebook, IDE, or production-pipeline style.

options.name: Jupyter exploratory profile
options.description: Jupyter notebooks are used primarily for exploratory analysis, validation, research, and sharing results rather than as a complete production-development environment.

options.name: IDE-and-notebook workflow profile
options.description: Python ML software is developed through an IDE and Jupyter notebooks, including notebook-oriented production workflows and direct cell-based query execution.

options.name: Governed mixed-language notebook-platform profile
options.description: Data science is conducted in a governed RStudio-based platform while retaining R as an implementation language and Jupyter or extended notebook tooling for exploratory work.

options.name: Scripted-production notebook-tooling profile
options.description: Exploration remains notebook-based, while production execution uses Python scripts and notebook work is supported by linting, alternative notebook tooling, and—where applicable—cell-based query execution.

options.name: Hard-coded notebook SQL
options.description: Embed fixed SQL queries directly in notebook cells.

options.name: Test-driven pipeline development
options.description: Production data pipelines are developed with tests, fixtures, and software-engineering practices.

options.name: Automated CI and testing validation
options.description: Validate ML changes through continuous integration and automated testing suites.

options.name: Target-infrastructure compatibility verification
options.description: Verify that ML code, packages, images, and runtime resources are compatible with the target production infrastructure.

options.name: Predictive-performance deployment gate
options.description: Require model performance evidence before promoting a model into production service.

options.name: Continuous testing as sole lifecycle practice
options.description: Rely on continuous testing without continuous training and validation for ML lifecycle assurance.

options.name: Development-production reproducibility parity
options.description: Development and production dependencies, procedures, and model inputs are kept equivalent to reproduce results reliably.

options.name: High-coverage preparation testing
options.description: Data preparation pipelines are developed with extensive automated testing and code coverage.

options.name: Dataset profiling and validation
options.description: Profile attributes, visualize distributions, analyze correlations, identify targets, and run data-quality checks before modeling.

options.name: Iterative bidirectional process model
options.description: Data-science work follows an iterative process in which phases can be revisited and refined.

options.name: Process-architecture separation
options.description: Treating process modeling as separate from technology and non-functional architectural decisions is rejected.

options.name: Flexible data-science process
options.description: The process model accommodates rapidly changing data-science technologies and requirements.

options.name: Production engineering and DevOps omission
options.description: Notebook-centered development omits production engineering and DevOps practices.

options.name: No continuous integration
options.description: Use a workflow without continuous integration because model changes are infrequent.

options.name: No continuous delivery
options.description: Use a workflow without continuous delivery because model releases are infrequent.

options.name: Semi-automated environment promotion
options.description: Deploy automatically to test environments while promoting manually or semi-manually across higher environments.

options.name: Experimentation workflow orchestration
options.description: Iterative algorithm and modeling experiments are coordinated before producing pipeline code.

options.name: Code-reviewed ML model specifications
options.description: Training specifications undergo code review as part of the ML development process.

options.name: File-based model packaging
options.description: A model is packaged as a file and loaded by a model server.

options.name: Containerized model packaging
options.description: Models are packaged as container images for deployment to serving infrastructure.

options.name: Amalgamated standalone model package
options.description: A portable package bundling model logic and parameters into a standalone deployable representation.

options.name: PMML model interchange format
options.description: An XML-based standardized format for serializing models and pipelines for serving.

options.name: PFA scoring-engine format
options.description: A JSON-based executable scoring-engine representation for model deployment.

options.name: ONNX framework-independent format
options.description: A serialized interchange format enabling models to move across tools and compatible inference runtimes.

options.name: Framework-specific model serialization
options.description: Models are serialized in formats native to their training framework or runtime.

options.name: MLeap model bundle serialization
options.description: Pipelines are exported as MLeap bundles for real-time model-server inference.

options.name: Core ML model serialization
options.description: Models are serialized as native .mlmodel artifacts for Apple application deployment.

options.name: Cross-framework model conversion
options.description: Models trained in one framework are converted into the target deployment framework's artifact format.

options.name: Dependency-bundled model package
options.description: Bundle the model or ensemble with invocation code, dependencies, and required deployment assets.

options.name: Platform-managed API serving
options.description: A managed ML platform automatically exposes trained models through an API.

options.name: Model-as-a-Service deployment
options.description: A dedicated prediction service exposes a model independently from consuming applications.

options.name: Shadow, competing-model, and traffic-split deployment
options.description: Validate or operate model versions through shadowing, A/B traffic splitting, or simultaneous competing-model service.

options.name: Client-server model-serving architecture
options.description: Deploy predictions through a client-request and continuously available server-response architecture.

options.name: Retraining-or-rollback restoration strategy
options.description: Restore service by either retraining and redeploying or rolling back to the previous model version.

options.name: Model-as-Dependency serving
options.description: Deploy the model together with its consuming application as a build- and runtime dependency.

options.name: Precompute serving
options.description: Precompute predictions or model outputs for later consumption.

options.name: Model-on-demand serving
options.description: Make the model available within the runtime scope when predictions are requested.

options.name: Progressive canary rollout and rollback
options.description: Expose candidate models to selected users progressively, compare impact, promote after confirmation, and roll back on failure.

options.name: Direct offline-model deployment
options.description: Deploy an offline-trained model directly as a prediction service without additional retraining, validation, or delivery automation.

options.name: REST service endpoint
options.description: Consumers call a model through a REST-based prediction service that returns results on request.

options.name: Multi-protocol network service
options.description: Consumers access the model through a network service supporting both REST and socket-based interactions.

options.name: Direct user or developer access
options.description: Users or calling systems interact with the model through an API-oriented user interface or command-line interface.

options.name: BI-integrated front-end consumption
options.description: Model predictions are consumed through an application or front end that may expose an API or user interface, integrate with BI tooling, and post-process results before presentation.

options.name: Transient contextual inference service
options.description: A short-lived client connects to a network prediction service, supplies or obtains the inference context, receives a result, and disconnects.

options.name: Post-processed prediction service
options.description: A prediction service transforms or enriches model outputs, adds explanations, or applies domain-specific decision and fallback logic before returning them.

options.name: Authenticated model access
options.description: Authentication restricts model use to authorized users or systems.

options.name: Prediction-service contract and load access
options.description: Prediction APIs are accessed through contract checks, authentication, and operational load validation.

options.name: End-to-end MLOps platform
options.description: A unified platform automates the ML lifecycle from development through deployment and operations without requiring a broader architectural emphasis.

options.name: Integrated or composable MLOps ecosystem
options.description: An ecosystem combines platform or provider-suite capabilities with selected separately assembled tools, allowing the arrangement to be tailored to organizational needs.

options.name: Production-first MLOps architecture
options.description: A production-oriented arrangement designs operational requirements into the ML architecture from the outset, potentially combining platform, suite, and custom tooling capabilities.

options.name: Managed-service pipeline composition
options.description: ML capabilities are divided across separate managed services for processing, building, deployment, and operational monitoring, without prescribing finer-grained application modularity.

options.name: Managed modular pipeline architecture
options.description: Managed ML services are organized into explicitly modular architectural units, with the selected granularity determining how capabilities are grouped and maintained.

options.name: Network-composed staged monolith architecture
options.description: Cloud-based ML components communicate through service interfaces while training and serving remain separate stages; application functionality is retained in a shared codebase rather than split by business concern.

options.name: Hybrid business-service ML architecture
options.description: ML capabilities are composed as network-accessible services with separate training and serving, combining shared-codebase functionality with independently operating services organized around business concerns.

options.name: Pluggable decomposed algorithm architecture
options.description: Algorithmic capabilities are exposed as composable services or modules so that algorithms can be replaced and decomposed according to evolving sophistication, freshness, responsiveness, and other system needs.

options.name: Global monolithic dependency updates
options.description: Update all implementing code when a deeply nested monolithic dependency changes its function signature.

options.name: Legacy compatibility bridge
options.description: Preserve compatibility with changed monolithic dependencies through a bridge to legacy code.

options.name: Platform-orchestrated continuous delivery
options.description: ML deployments are coordinated through a container-orchestration platform, with continuous delivery workflows integrated into the platform. This option covers Kubernetes-based execution and delivery coordination across infrastructure.

options.name: Artifact-promoted continuous delivery
options.description: ML deployments are coordinated as continuous delivery workflows that build, validate, package, and promote deployable artifacts into target environments. The emphasis is on delivery-pipeline coordination rather than a specific infrastructure orchestrator.

options.name: Hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure
options.description: ML operations span cloud and retained on-premises infrastructure.

options.name: On-premises sensitive-data retention
options.description: Private and sensitive data remains on company servers instead of leaving the organizational boundary.

options.name: VM-hosted development environment
options.description: Host development tools and data access in virtual machines rather than on developer workstations.

options.name: Restricted direct analytical-data access
options.description: Do not grant plot consumers direct access to underlying data because of privacy and organizational constraints.

options.name: Secure non-local development access
options.description: Provide development access to protected data through a non-local hosted environment.

options.name: Self-built infrastructure
options.description: Organizations build and operate their own platform and infrastructure rather than buying a fully managed platform.

options.name: Fully managed platform
options.description: Organizations adopt a fully managed platform for infrastructure and ML operations.

options.name: Operations-owned production environment
options.description: Assign production-environment operation to dedicated operations professionals.

options.name: Outsourced ML capability
options.description: Use external providers instead of building all ML expertise and capability internally.

options.name: ML capability restructuring
options.description: Restructure the organization to obtain the expertise needed to integrate ML into products.

options.name: Problem de-scoping for limited ML expertise
options.description: Reduce the ML problem scope when the organization cannot afford required data-science expertise.

options.name: Separated ML and application responsibilities
options.description: Assign model complexity to data scientists and user-experience complexity to application developers.

options.name: Hybrid data-science and software-engineering team
options.description: Combine data scientists or ML researchers with software engineers whose production responsibilities and experience differ.

options.name: AI-assisted IT operations automation
options.description: Use big data and machine learning to monitor IT operations, identify issues, and trigger proactive responses.

options.name: AIOps–MLOps interchangeability
options.description: Treat AIOps and MLOps as interchangeable operational approaches.

options.name: Basic production performance monitoring
options.description: Operational signals track deployed-model performance, live behavior, drift, and data-quality issues over time, without necessarily adding broader diagnostic mechanisms.

options.name: Health-augmented production monitoring
options.description: Production performance and data-quality monitoring is augmented with model and service health checks, operational diagnostics, and related runtime signals.

options.name: Consistency- and dependency-aware monitoring
options.description: Monitoring additionally validates training-serving consistency and observes external data dependencies that can affect deployed behavior.

options.name: Comprehensive production observability
options.description: An integrated monitoring arrangement combines performance, health, consistency, dependency, and persisted prediction evidence for ongoing assessment and comparison.

options.name: Consistency and prediction-evidence monitoring
options.description: Monitoring combines production behavior with training-serving consistency checks, dependency signals, and persisted live or candidate predictions for later analysis.

options.name: Multi-criteria model oversight
options.description: Operational oversight considers stability, ethics, fairness, explainability, user experience, edge cases, and accuracy.

options.name: Single error-minimization objective
options.description: Reducing all operational, ethical, and user concerns to one error-minimization objective is rejected.

options.name: Human-machine production oversight
options.description: Production systems combine automated model behavior with continuing human intervention.

options.name: Human review and feedback for low-confidence predictions
options.description: Low-confidence outputs are reviewed by people and labeled results feed later retraining.

options.name: Additional user verification
options.description: Email confirmation and two-factor authentication add human or product verification to mitigate account takeover.

options.name: Single shared optimization metric
options.description: Align machine-learning and product teams around one primary metric for optimization.

options.name: Regulatory and business alignment
options.description: MLOps practices align deployed models with organizational needs and regulatory requirements.

options.name: Explicit monitoring ownership assignment
options.description: Monitoring responsibility is assigned to a named role or coordinated set of stakeholders after deployment.

options.name: Unassigned long-term monitoring responsibility
options.description: No clear owner remains responsible for monitoring after the model creator moves to other work.

options.name: Operational value realization
options.description: Models are moved into operational use to solve business problems and generate measurable value. The emphasis is on deployment and sustained use rather than on broader adoption practices.

options.name: Stakeholder-engaged production adoption
options.description: Models are brought into production through stakeholder participation, transparent communication, and alignment with organizational goals. This approach combines operational use with active engagement of affected parties.

options.name: Collaborative, transparent production adoption
options.description: Models are sustained in production through stakeholder engagement, transparent monitoring or communication, and shared collaboration mechanisms. This is the most comprehensive adoption approach, connecting operational value with enterprise collaboration.

options.name: Repository-based asset sharing
options.description: Teams share and reuse ML assets through a common repository, with repository access serving as the primary collaboration mechanism.

options.name: Guided cross-language code reuse
options.description: Teams reuse code across languages and frameworks under architectural guidance, while other collaboration practices remain separate concerns.

options.name: Documented collaborative repositories
options.description: Teams collaboratively develop and reuse assets in a shared repository while applying minimum documentation practices to improve traceability and reproducibility.

options.name: Governed full-lifecycle asset collaboration
options.description: Teams use a shared, documented and collaboratively maintained asset ecosystem that also supports guided code reuse and maintainable implementations.

options.name: Documented collaborative development
options.description: Teams collaboratively develop ML assets with minimum documentation standards, without the repository or cross-language reuse practices being the defining mechanism.

options.name: Forced R-language porting
options.description: Requiring code to be ported to R is rejected as an inflexible enterprise-architecture practice.

options.name: Comprehensive ML artifact versioning
options.description: Source code, datasets, models, schemas, executables, and dependencies are versioned and retained through version-control and artifact-management systems to support reproducibility.

options.name: Source-controlled pipeline versioning
options.description: ML pipeline and application source code is versioned and retained, while other ML artifacts are not necessarily managed as versioned assets.

options.name: Solution architect oversight
options.description: A solution architect or lead data scientist ensures non-functional requirements are addressed.

options.name: Predefined architecture and process framework
options.description: A predefined framework guides architectural decisions and systematic treatment of non-functional requirements.

options.name: Automated model-family selection
options.description: AutoML selects among alternative model families as part of pipeline construction.

options.name: Model ensembling
options.description: Multiple models are combined to improve predictive stability or score.

options.name: Explicit model-objective prioritization
options.description: Teams choose which quality objective, such as false-negative minimization, to optimize.

options.name: Boxed machine-learning solutions
options.description: Prepackaged boxed solutions are rejected when their predictive scores are inadequate.

options.name: Rule-based solution
options.description: Use predefined business rules instead of a learned model when they already meet objectives.

options.name: Machine learning for an already solvable problem
options.description: Adopt machine learning despite an existing classical solution meeting business objectives.

options.name: Manual hyperparameter tuning
options.description: Practitioners tune model hyperparameters by hand and trial and error for smaller modeling tasks.

options.name: Automated hyperparameter optimization
options.description: Search procedures automatically optimize model hyperparameters when manual exploration is impractical.

options.name: Neural architecture search
options.description: Automated search designs neural network architectures instead of relying entirely on manual architecture construction.

options.name: Heuristic fraud prediction
options.description: Recognized repetitive patterns are handled with manually defined heuristics for fraud prediction.

options.name: Machine-learning fraud detection
options.description: Machine learning handles complex and evolving fraud vectors beyond practical heuristic rules.

options.name: XGBoost model training
options.description: XGBoost is selected as the model-building algorithm for training.

options.name: Notebook-managed result caching
options.description: Notebook execution automatically retains cell results and variables for reuse until explicitly cleared or recomputed.

options.name: Application-managed persistent caching
options.description: Applications explicitly persist reusable computation results in files, buckets, or databases.

options.name: ElastiCache model state
options.description: Current model parameters and inference features are retrieved from an in-memory store.

options.name: Intermediate artifact pointer tracking
options.description: Execution state records locations of intermediate data, statistics, vocabularies, anomalies, and models.

options.name: Pipeline resumption from completed steps
options.description: A failed pipeline resumes after its latest completed step instead of recomputing successful work.

options.name: Traditional model-parameter store
options.description: Use a traditional relational or NoSQL store for rapidly changing model parameters.

options.name: Artifact versioning
options.description: Versioned data inputs, generated models, and pipeline artifacts are recorded to support reproducibility and controlled reuse.

options.name: Integrated experiment and artifact tracking
options.description: Experiments and training runs are organized with their metrics, metadata, and versioned artifacts so that candidate models can be compared and reproduced.

options.name: Comprehensive pipeline lifecycle tracking
options.description: A metadata-backed system captures pipeline executions, metrics, experiments, lineage, parameters, and versioned artifacts across the ML lifecycle.

options.name: Online-learning telemetry tracking
options.description: Online-learning systems retain incoming examples and predictions together with execution metadata and evaluation metrics, enabling replay, debugging, and counterfactual analysis.

options.name: Incremental linear learning
options.description: Linear or logistic learners update rapidly from incoming examples for online learning.

options.name: Stochastic-gradient optimization
options.description: Stochastic-gradient methods update model parameters incrementally as training examples arrive.

options.name: Atomic model-parameter updates
options.description: Model parameter retrieval and updates are performed atomically so predictions never observe partial state.

options.name: Periodic model-parameter persistence
options.description: Learned parameters are periodically persisted so real-time prediction workers can use current model state.

options.name: Atomic model-parameter access
options.description: Retrieve the model state atomically before calculating a prediction.

options.name: FIFO training-data queue
options.description: Randomly arriving examples are delivered through a first-in-first-out queue.

options.name: Buffered and shuffled training-data queue
options.description: Examples are buffered and shuffled before queue insertion when the source stream is not random.

options.name: Redis queue primitives
options.description: General-purpose Redis list operations provide queueing for training data and shared system state.

options.name: Dedicated training-data message broker
options.description: A specialized message broker provides queue management for incoming training data.

options.name: Mixed-mode parallel feature computation
options.description: Features are generated through a combination of asynchronous processing, synchronous precomputed queries, and parallel feature queries. This mode supports multiple timing paths while reducing latency for time-sensitive predictions.

options.name: Hybrid asynchronous and precomputed feature computation
options.description: Features are produced asynchronously when short delays are acceptable and retrieved synchronously from precomputed results when decisions must respond immediately. This mode does not require parallel feature-query execution.

options.name: Batch processing
options.description: Process data as discrete jobs or recurring offline runs.

options.name: Real-time processing
options.description: Process data continuously with minimal delay while it moves through the pipeline.

options.name: Near-real-time processing
options.description: Process data with delays of several seconds to several minutes.

options.name: Industry forecast workflow
options.description: Use historical-data forecasting as a production workflow for industry systems.

options.name: Offline versus real-time execution placement
options.description: Risk workloads execute offline or in real time according to urgency and computational requirements.

options.name: Analytical warehouse or lake storage
options.description: Use a data warehouse or data lake as the final analytical store for ML and analytics data.

options.name: OLAP or analytics-database storage
options.description: Use an OLAP system or analytics database as the final analytical store.

options.name: Integrated SQL-and-distributed analytical access
options.description: Retrieve and process analytical data through a combined access approach that supports both SQL-oriented tools and distributed query or processing frameworks.

options.name: Distributed framework analytical access
options.description: Retrieve and process analytical data primarily through distributed query or processing frameworks, without an explicitly integrated SQL-based access approach.
